clue.text: Use stick to turn up ground where there's disease

parts.note: to club is to hit with a stick, so using a stick on something is clubbing it
to root is to dig up soil with the snout, as a pig does

explanation.surface: A gardener jabs at the soil with a stick to see where a plant infection has struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubroot is a fungal infection that swells and distorts the roots of cabbages and other brassicas.

clue.text: Left track, going over lakes to one town on bay

indicators.note: in a down entry the track sits above the lakes, passing over them

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track or road
L abbreviates lake, so LL is lakes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves a path, crossing lakes on the way to a coastal town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' puts LANE above LL in the down entry; doubling an abbreviation makes a plural, so LL is lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in south Wales that stands on Carmarthen Bay.

clue.text: Country song, swell at first, but lacking finish

indicators.note: the shortened swell is placed at the front, before the song
the word for swell is missing its last letter

parts.note: to swell is to bulge outward
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A country tune that builds at the start but has no proper ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' looks like the definition, a genre of music, but 'Country' alone defines and 'song' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a nation in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Not in form, but show clear superiority

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a class or form is a group of pupils in a school year

explanation.surface: A sportsperson out of form still manages to dominate opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in form' reads as one idea, poor form, but splits in two; 'form' is a school year group, British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass rivals is to be far better than them, plainly superior.

clue.text: Set that got divinely stoned on a couple of tablets

definitions.text: Set that got divinely stoned on a couple of tablets

parts.words: Set that got divinely stoned on a couple of tablets
parts.note: sounds like a group high on drugs, but describes a set of laws God carved in stone on two tablets for Moses

explanation.surface: A crowd who got blissfully high on a couple of pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' and 'tablets' suggest drugs, but the tablets are the two stone slabs given to Moses on Mount Sinai.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical laws given by God to Moses were inscribed on two tablets of stone.

clue.text: Instrument captivating a really big composer

indicators.note: the instrument holds the a captive inside it

parts.note: a grand is a grand piano
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for very large

explanation.surface: A huge musician holds a piano enthralled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big composer' tempts as one idea, but 'really big' is the clothing label for outsize, a British size marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrique Granados was a Spanish composer and pianist, known for the piano suite Goyescas.

clue.text: Music requiring study — Ill support sure-fire winner

indicators.note: in a down entry the speaker sits below the winner, holding it up

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a cert is a certainty, a horse sure to win
printed for I'll, I will: the I is the speaker

explanation.surface: A performer, needing to practise, vows to back a racehorse that cannot lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill' is the OCR form of I'll; 'support' puts I below CERT in the down entry. CERT is British slang for a dead certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti are musical works for a solo instrument and orchestra, pieces of classical music.

clue.text: Detected first person to intrude over private lands

indicators.note: the first person pushes into the middle of the turned word
in a down entry, over means the word for detected is turned upside down

parts.note: to detect is to sense, so detected is sensed
me is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An intruder is spotted trespassing on private estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for detected upside down in this down entry, making DESNES, before the first person goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord for his own use, a private estate.

clue.text: All that Tiny Tim wanted a blessing on

definitions.text: All that Tiny Tim wanted a blessing on

parts.words: All that Tiny Tim wanted a blessing on
parts.note: Tiny Tim's famous toast in Dickens's A Christmas Carol asks God to bless us all, each and every person

explanation.surface: A question about whom the little boy in Dickens wished God to bless.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim is the sick child in Dickens's A Christmas Carol; his closing line is 'God bless Us, Every One!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the toast also means all people without exception, matching 'All'.

clue.text: Dividing up Scottish pattern, line a muslin

indicators.note: the line and the a split the Scottish pattern into two parts by sitting between its letters

parts.note: tartan is the chequered pattern of Scottish clan cloth

explanation.surface: A dressmaker lines a muslin garment with a strip of Scottish check cut into sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dividing up' is the container signal: L and A go into the middle of TARTAN, giving TAR-LA-TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarlatan is a thin, open-weave stiffened cotton fabric, a kind of muslin used for ball gowns.

clue.text: Wow! Perfect place for seaside drive

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
a niche is a position perfectly suited to someone, as in finding one's niche

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation about the ideal spot for a drive along the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is everyday British slang for 'wow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a coastal road cut along a cliff face, as on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Women's quarters in gaol rise in revolt

indicators.note: a revolt turns things upside down, so these letters are overthrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Inmates of a prison rise up in rebellion inside the women's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' signals an anagram of GAOL RISE; 'gaol' is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the harem of a Muslim palace, where the wives and concubines lived.

clue.text: Member of establishment staff taking risks, cut short

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it, a verb

indicators.note: the word for taking risks has its final letter lopped off

parts.note: daring describes someone bold enough to take risks

explanation.surface: An employee of an institution is disciplined for reckless behaviour and has their hours reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is a verb here, giving MAN; 'cut short' removes the last letter of DARING to give DARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a senior, influential official, a powerful figure in the civil service or establishment.

clue.text: Three numbers summing to one figure

definitions.text: Three numbers summing to one figure

parts.words: Three numbers summing to one figure
parts.note: reads like arithmetic, adding three values to a total, but means the bust, waist and hip measurements that describe a body's shape

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle in which three values add up to a single total.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'figure' is a person's shape, not a digit, and the three numbers are bust, waist and hip measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the informal term for a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements, which together describe her shape.

clue.text: Treacherous girl has to die

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A girl must die for her betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: VI is a girl's name (short for Violet), a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Viperish describes spiteful, venomous behaviour, as of someone who might betray you like a snake.

clue.text: Satirise ridiculous old prophet

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so the word is thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A command to lampoon a silly ancient seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' signals an anagram of SATIRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresias was the blind seer of Thebes in Greek myth, who foretold the fate of Oedipus.

clue.text: Lydia dramatised end of trivial suffering

indicators.note: the end of the word trivial is its final letter

parts.note: anguish is severe suffering

explanation.surface: Someone dramatises a trivial complaint, making a show of suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes L from 'trivial'. 'Lydia' looks like any name but points to a stage heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia Languish is the romantic heroine of Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, a character brought to the stage.

clue.text: For example, pans what Clausewitz wrote in high passion

indicators.note: the title sits inside the word for high passion

parts.note: ire is strong anger, a high passion
Carl von Clausewitz wrote the military treatise translated as On War

explanation.surface: A military theorist's writing is described as cooking pots full of fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ON WAR, the English title of Clausewitz's Vom Kriege, inside IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironware is goods made of iron, and pans are one example of such kitchen items.

clue.text: House number, repeated wrongly, holds me up

indicators.note: the jumbled pair grips the word me inside it
the doubled number is set down in the wrong order
the number is used twice over

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A house number written down twice incorrectly causes a delay for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' gives TENTEN; 'wrongly' rearranges it to TENENT; 'holds' puts ME inside, TENE-ME-NT. 'up' just completes 'holds up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into flats, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Caller is redirected in city

indicators.note: something redirected is sent along a different course, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A telephone call is rerouted within a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' signals an anagram of CALLER IS. Carlisle is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a cathedral city in Cumbria, near the Scottish border.

clue.text: Soldier without papers? That's extremely suspicious

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
having no identity documents means having no ID

explanation.surface: A soldier caught with no documents strikes the officials as highly suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: PARA is a paratrooper; 'without papers' gives NO ID, no identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranoid person is irrationally distrustful, always suspecting others of plotting against them.

clue.text: Polite German writer in good time to knock out article

parts.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist, author of Death in Venice

indicators.note: the article is struck out of the phrase meaning in good time

parts.note: arriving early is arriving in good time
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A courteous German author always arrives punctually but drops a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock out' removes A, an article, from EARLY, leaving ERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mannerly has good manners, behaving courteously and politely.

clue.text: Find a new supplier for useful device

definitions.meaning: to source something again from another provider, a verb
a means or expedient that one can draw on in difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: To source again is to obtain from a new supplier, and a ready expedient or asset is a means one can call on.

clue.text: Clear about regions in one part of the world

indicators.note: the word for clear goes around the outside of the word for regions

parts.note: to clear a sum as profit is to net it
areas are regions

explanation.surface: Making a clean sweep across zones in one corner of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' is the verb for making a profit, not 'transparent', and the regions sit between its first two letters and its last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is the region around the eastern Mediterranean, from Turkey to Egypt.

clue.text: Quickly recorded view — stable's original tips extremely reliable

indicators.note: the original part of the word stable is its first letter

parts.note: in racing a nap is a tipster's most confident selection of the day
a hot tip or hot favourite is one thought very likely to win

explanation.surface: A racing stable's first confident tips for the day are captured in a hasty glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' picks S from 'stable's'; a NAP is a racing tipster's best bet, and HOT is a very sure tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a photograph taken quickly and informally, a fleeting record of a scene.

clue.text: Pleasant exercises leading to a bloom

parts.note: sweet means pleasant or agreeable
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Agreeable workouts lead to a flower blossoming.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is British school gym lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden plant grown for its fragrant flowers.
